```plato
//==
// # Differential geometry
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Differential geometry: moving frames and jets
//  - Geodesics and curvature visualization
//  - Differential geometry: surface points and curvature

//==
// # Differential geometry: moving frames and jets
//
// Local frames carried along curves, and the raw derivative jets from which
// those frames and their curvatures are computed. Lengths are in world units,
// curvatures and torsions in reciprocal world units, and derivatives are taken
// with respect to the curve or surface parameter.

//==
// # Moving frames along curves

// The Frenet frame of a planar curve at one parameter value: position, unit
// tangent, unit left normal, and signed curvature (reciprocal world units;
// positive when the curve bends toward the normal).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curvature)
type FrenetFrame2D
    implements IValue
{
    Position: Point2D;
    Tangent: Direction2D;
    Normal: Direction2D;
    Curvature: Number;
}

// The Frenet-Serret frame of a space curve at one parameter value. Curvature is
// nonnegative (reciprocal world units); torsion (reciprocal world units) measures
// how fast the osculating plane rotates about the tangent. Undefined where
// curvature vanishes.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frenet%E2%80%93Serret_formulas)
type FrenetFrame3D
    implements IValue
{
    Position: Point3D;
    Tangent: Direction3D;
    Normal: Direction3D;
    Binormal: Direction3D;
    Curvature: Number;
    Torsion: Number;
}

// A rotation-minimizing (parallel-transport) frame sample along a space curve.
// Unlike the Frenet frame it stays stable through inflections and straight runs.
// Parameter is the curve parameter at which the frame was sampled (unit-agnostic).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallel_transport)
type RotationMinimizingFrame3D
    implements IValue
{
    Position: Point3D;
    Tangent: Direction3D;
    Normal: Direction3D;
    Binormal: Direction3D;
    Parameter: Number;
}

// The Darboux frame of a curve lying on a surface: curve tangent, surface normal,
// and tangent normal (surface normal cross tangent). Normal and geodesic
// curvatures are in reciprocal world units; geodesic torsion likewise.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darboux_frame)
type DarbouxFrame3D
    implements IValue
{
    Position: Point3D;
    Tangent: Direction3D;
    SurfaceNormal: Direction3D;
    TangentNormal: Direction3D;
    NormalCurvature: Number;
    GeodesicCurvature: Number;
    GeodesicTorsion: Number;
}

//==
// # Derivative jets
//
// Raw positional derivatives from which frames and curvature are computed.
// Derivatives are with respect to the parameter: world units per parameter unit,
// per squared parameter unit, and so on.

// A second-order jet of a planar curve: position plus first and second
// parametric derivatives at Parameter.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jet_(mathematics))
type CurveJet2D
    implements IValue
{
    Parameter: Number;
    Position: Point2D;
    FirstDerivative: Vector2D;
    SecondDerivative: Vector2D;
}

// A third-order jet of a space curve: position plus first, second, and third
// parametric derivatives at Parameter. Third order is enough for torsion.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torsion_of_a_curve)
type CurveJet3D
    implements IValue
{
    Parameter: Number;
    Position: Point3D;
    FirstDerivative: Vector3D;
    SecondDerivative: Vector3D;
    ThirdDerivative: Vector3D;
}

// A second-order jet of a parametric surface at Uv: position, both first
// partial derivatives, and the three second partials.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parametric_surface)
type SurfaceJet3D
    implements IValue
{
    Uv: UvCoordinate;
    Position: Point3D;
    DerivativeU: Vector3D;
    DerivativeV: Vector3D;
    DerivativeUU: Vector3D;
    DerivativeUV: Vector3D;
    DerivativeVV: Vector3D;
}

//==
// # Geodesics and curvature visualization
//
// Traced shortest paths on surfaces, and the sampled constructions used to show
// curvature to a reader: osculating circles and curvature combs. Lengths and
// radii are in world units; curvature is in reciprocal world units.

// A geodesic (locally shortest path) traced on a surface, approximated as a
// polyline of surface points. TotalLength is the arc length in world units.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geodesic)
type GeodesicPath3D
{
    Points: Array<Point3D>;
    TotalLength: Number;
}

// The osculating circle of a planar curve at a point: the circle of best
// second-order contact. Radius (world units) is the reciprocal of the unsigned
// curvature at ContactPoint.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osculating_circle)
type OsculatingCircle2D
    implements IValue
{
    Center: Point2D;
    Radius: Number;
    ContactPoint: Point2D;
}
```
